headline: Highest risk is medium: shared MCP/API-style interaction can enable prompt injection, data leakage, and output-cascade, but no direct shared workspace or documented pairwise exploit is shown.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher can ingest web/file content and exposes MCP plus browser/file surfaces; MemMachine also exposes MCP and is designed to connect through REST/SDK/MCP. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if one agent’s outputs are fed into the other, though no direct exploit is documented here.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher output is passed into MemMachine as MCP/REST input without provenance filtering
IF MemMachine returns user-memory text that gpt-researcher later parses as instructions
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all inter-agent messages
Strip imperative language before forwarding outputs
Disable MCP bridging between the two agents
Require a human review step for any agent-generated instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher touches local documents, citations, images, and multiple API keys; MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. If they share an MCP or workspace bridge, sensitive research material could flow into memory or context, but the profiles do not show a shared filesystem or direct data path.
conditions: IF research documents or citations from gpt-researcher are forwarded into MemMachine memory
IF MemMachine context is exported back into gpt-researcher prompts or reports
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Redact secrets before any handoff
Turn off persistence for shared sessions
Limit MemMachine inputs to summaries only

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-researcher has broad filesystem and subprocess capabilities, while MemMachine exposes allowlisted network egress and MCP. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same directory or shared mutable resource, so conflict risk is present only if an operator wires them to the same state.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same shared directory or database
IF an orchestrator gives both agents mutable access to the same MCP-backed resource
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Use per-agent credentials
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Enable file locking on shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is explicitly a planner/execution/publisher style research agent, and MemMachine is a conversational memory layer that can feed context back into downstream prompts. If MemMachine treats gpt-researcher output as authoritative, errors can cascade into later travel-planning responses; no verification step is documented in the profiles.
conditions: IF MemMachine stores gpt-researcher output as trusted memory
IF downstream travel-planning prompts reuse that memory without verification
mitigations: Require citations on all research claims
Add a verification prompt before memory writes
Mark agent-generated facts as untrusted
Limit memory writes to user-approved facts only

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher handles API keys and local documents, while MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. The profiles do not show a residency mismatch, regulated data class, or retention-policy conflict, so compliance risk is limited to general policy alignment rather than a specific breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed into either agent
IF the operator requires a retention or deletion policy that the pair cannot enforce
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to either agent
Document retention settings for both systems
Separate personal memory from research artifacts
Review vendor data-processing terms
